manifest_row.title: Continuous finite-dimensional ordered-simplex integrals
manifest_row.design_state: Root-authorized local C0 simplex-integration helper; proof authored; ordinary native review and current metadata pending.
manifest_row.statement:
Let $T\geq0$, let $n\geq0$ be an integer, and let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real or complex vector space with a specified finite ordered basis and its coordinate topology. Put $D_n(T)=\{0\leq s_1\leq\cdots\leq s_n\leq T\}$, with $D_0(T)=\{()\}$. Let $F:D_n(T)\to V$ have continuous coordinates. Set $G_0=F$. For $1\leq k\leq n$, write $y=(s_{k+1},\ldots,s_n)\in D_{n-k}(T)$ and put $b_k(y)=s_{k+1}$ if $k<n$, and $b_n(())=T$. Define recursively
$$
G_k(y)=\int_0^{b_k(y)}G_{k-1}(s_k,y)\,ds_k,
$$
integrating real coordinates, and real and imaginary parts of complex coordinates. Every integral exists and every $G_k$ is continuous on its remaining parameter domain. Write $I_n(F)=G_n(())$; equivalently this is the iterated integral with limits $0\leq s_1\leq\cdots\leq s_n\leq T$. Degenerate one-variable integrals are zero. For $n=0$, set $I_0(F)=F(())$; for $n\geq1$ and $T=0$, $I_n(F)=0$.

These integrals are linear, independent of the chosen finite basis, and commute with finite-dimensional linear maps. For any norm $\|\cdot\|$ on $V$, the corresponding one-variable integral satisfies $\|\int_a^b g(s)\,ds\|\leq\int_a^b\|g(s)\|\,ds$ for continuous $g$ and $a\leq b$. If $\|F(s)\|\leq C$ on $D_n(T)$, where $C\geq0$, then
$$
\|I_n(F)\|\leq C\frac{T^n}{n!}.
$$
Here the factor for $n=0$ is $1$, including $T=0$. For scalar $F=1$, $I_n(1)=T^n/n!$ with this convention. For real scalar $F\geq0$, every partial integral $G_k$ is nonnegative. No differentiability of $F$ or choice principle is assumed.

manifest_statement.expected:
Let $d\geq1$, let $r\geq0$ be an integer, let $H=H^*\in M_d(\mathbb C)$ have units joules, let $\hbar>0$ have units joule-seconds, and let $L_1,\ldots,L_r\in M_d(\mathbb C)$ have units $\mathrm{s}^{-1/2}$, with the finite GKSL convention of [[def-qsm-dt-gksl-definition]]. Put $K=-iH/\hbar-\frac12\sum_{a=1}^rL_a^*L_a$ and $R(u)=e^{uK}$ for $u\geq0$, with the exponential defined by its norm-convergent power series. For a density matrix $\rho\in M_d(\mathbb C)$, meaning $\rho=\rho^*\geq0$ and $\operatorname{Tr}\rho=1$, define the no-jump branch at time $t\geq0$ by $W_{\varnothing,\varnothing}(t)=R(t)$ and its branch state by $W_{\varnothing,\varnothing}(t)\rho W_{\varnothing,\varnothing}(t)^*$.

All time variables $u,t,s_1,\ldots,s_n$ are measured in seconds. For $n\geq1$, a jump-history label is $\mathbf a=(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\in\{1,\ldots,r\}^n$ and its jump times are seconds $0<s_1<\cdots<s_n<t$. Define the corresponding branch operator by $W_{\mathbf a,\mathbf s}(t)=R(t-s_n)L_{a_n}R(s_n-s_{n-1})\cdots L_{a_2}R(s_2-s_1)L_{a_1}R(s_1)$ and the unnormalized branch state by $W_{\mathbf a,\mathbf s}(t)\rho W_{\mathbf a,\mathbf s}(t)^*$. Its branch-weight density is $w_{\mathbf a,\mathbf s}(t)=\operatorname{Tr}(W_{\mathbf a,\mathbf s}(t)\rho W_{\mathbf a,\mathbf s}(t)^*)$. The ordered-simplex integral of this density means the repeated Riemann integral $\int_0^t ds_n\int_0^{s_n}ds_{n-1}\cdots\int_0^{s_2}ds_1$, applied componentwise to matrices; each continuous real component is integrable on the compact integration interval. For $n\geq1$, $W_{\mathbf a,\mathbf s}$ has units $\mathrm{s}^{-n/2}$ and $w_{\mathbf a,\mathbf s}$ has units $\mathrm{s}^{-n}$; integrating over the $n$ time variables gives a dimensionless weight. If $r=0$, there are no branches with $n\geq1$. This definition alone does not assert that the branch weights sum to one.

For a density matrix $\rho\in M_d(\mathbb C)$, meaning $\rho=\rho^*\geq0$ and $\operatorname{Tr}\rho=1$, define the no-jump branch at time $t\geq0$ by $W_{\varnothing,\varnothing}(t)=R(t)$ and its branch state by $W_{\varnothing,\varnothing}(t)\rho W_{\varnothing,\varnothing}(t)^*$.

All time variables $u,t,s_1,\ldots,s_n$ are measured in seconds. For $n\geq1$, a jump-history label is $\mathbf a=(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\in\{1,\ldots,r\}^n$ and its jump times are seconds $0<s_1<\cdots<s_n<t$. Its branch-weight density is the real-valued scalar function $w_{\mathbf a,\mathbf s}(t)=\operatorname{Tr}(W_{\mathbf a,\mathbf s}(t)\rho W_{\mathbf a,\mathbf s}(t)^*)$. For $n\geq1$, let $\overline{\Delta}_n(t)=\{(s_1,\ldots,s_n)\in\mathbb R^n:0\leq s_1\leq\cdots\leq s_n\leq t\}$ and $\Delta_n(t)=\{(s_1,\ldots,s_n)\in\mathbb R^n:0<s_1<\cdots<s_n<t\}$. Use the same formula for $W_{\mathbf a,\mathbf s}(t)$ on $\overline{\Delta}_n(t)$; it is continuous there because $R(u)=e^{uK}$ is continuous for $u\geq0$. If $V$ is a finite-dimensional real or complex vector space and $F:\overline{\Delta}_n(t)\to V$ has continuous coordinates in a basis, define $\int_{\Delta_n(t)}F(\mathbf s)\,d\mathbf s$ as exactly the repeated one-variable Riemann integral over the closed limits shown here $\int_0^t ds_n\int_0^{s_n}ds_{n-1}\cdots\int_0^{s_2}F(s_1,\ldots,s_n)\,ds_1$, integrating each real coordinate; for complex coordinates, integrate their real and imaginary parts separately. This value is independent of the basis because a change of basis is a finite linear combination and scalar Riemann integration is linear. For $V=\mathbb R$ this defines the scalar integral of the density $w_{\mathbf a,\mathbf s}(t)$; the same convention applies to branch-state integrands with values in $M_d(\mathbb C)$ and to integrands with values in the finite-dimensional complex vector space of complex-linear maps $M_d(\mathbb C)\to M_d(\mathbb C)$. The full recursion is well-defined for these arbitrary continuous integrands by [[lem-nrqmx-continuous-simplex-integrals]]: every inner integral is continuous in all remaining ordered parameters, so the next integral exists. That lemma also proves basis independence, linear-map commutation, the norm bound by the supremum times $t^n/n!$, and positivity for nonnegative real scalar integrands. Set $\int_a^a f(s)\,ds=0$ for a degenerate interval; hence every $n\geq1$ ordered-simplex integral at $t=0$ is zero. Let $\Delta_0(t)=\{()\}$ and define $\int_{\Delta_0(t)}F=F(())$; in the expansion, the $n=0$ contribution is the no-jump branch already defined above. For $n\geq1$, $W_{\mathbf a,\mathbf s}$ has units $\mathrm{s}^{-n/2}$ and $w_{\mathbf a,\mathbf s}$ has units $\mathrm{s}^{-n}$; integrating over the $n$ time variables gives a dimensionless weight. If $r=0$, there are no branches with $n\geq1$. This definition alone does not assert that the branch weights sum to one.

manifest_statement.expected:
Let $d\geq1$, let $H=H^*\in M_d(\mathbb C)$ have units joules, let $\hbar>0$ have units joule-seconds, and let $L_1,\ldots,L_r\in M_d(\mathbb C)$ be a finite family with units $\mathrm{s}^{-1/2}$, where $r\geq0$. For the selected time-homogeneous finite GKSL model, put $\mathcal L(X)=-\frac{i}{\hbar}[H,X]+\sum_{a=1}^r(L_aXL_a^*-\frac12\{L_a^*L_a,X\})$. With $K=-iH/\hbar-\frac12\sum_aL_a^*L_a$ and the finite branch operators of [[def-nrqmx-finite-jump-trajectories]], each no-jump operator $R(u)=e^{uK}$ is a contraction, each branch state $W_{\mathbf a,\mathbf s}(t)\rho W_{\mathbf a,\mathbf s}(t)^*$ is positive for $\rho\geq0$, and for every density matrix $\rho$ and $t\geq0$,

$$e^{t\mathcal L}(\rho)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\ \sum_{\mathbf a\in\{1,\ldots,r\}^n}\ \int_{0<s_1<\cdots<s_n<t}W_{\mathbf a,\mathbf s}(t)\rho W_{\mathbf a,\mathbf s}(t)^*\,ds_1\cdots ds_n,$$

where the $n=0$ term is $R(t)\rho R(t)^*$ and branches with $n\geq1$ are absent when $r=0$. The series converges in trace norm, uniformly on each bounded time interval; the sum of all branch weights is one. This is an ensemble representation of the finite GKSL solution, not a unique microscopic trajectory or a claim about a particular detector.
